_comment: Explicitly accepted dependency-scanner findings. Anything listed here is
known, justified, and will NOT fail the build; anything not listed that
meets the gating threshold WILL fail it. See cmd/vulngate + tools/vulngate
and docs/adr/0011-ci-pipeline-and-security-gating.md.
Gating threshold: npm audit high + critical; govulncheck 'called' (the Go
vuln DB carries no CVSS severity, so reachability is the signal).
Every entry needs a real reason — vulngate rejects a baseline entry with
an empty reason, so a silent suppression is not possible. Include the date
and revisit entries when the upstream fix lands.
As of 2026-08-05 this list was EMPTY with the npm side measured (0
vulnerabilities at every severity) and the GO SIDE UNMEASURED, because
vuln.go.dev is blocked by this project's development environment. That
note said the first CI run on an agent with normal network access would
establish the real Go baseline, and that pre-existing 'called' findings
should be added here with reasons rather than weakening the gate.
That run happened on 2026-10-18 (the first run of the GitHub Actions
pipeline, on PR #347). It reported 155 gating findings, which were EIGHT
distinct advisories repeated once per call site:
google.golang.org/grpc     GO-2026-6348, -6443
golang.org/x/text          GO-2026-5970, -6629
All eight were FIXED rather than baselined, so this list is still empty
and is now empty on both halves as a measured result:
go.mod `go 1.25.0` -> `go 1.26.9`  (the four net/http advisories are
HTTP/2 server bugs whose only fix
is a toolchain >= go1.26.9)
google.golang.org/grpc  -> v1.83.2 (6348 needs >= v1.83.1, 6443 >= v1.83.2)
golang.org/x/net        -> v0.60.0 (not reported, since this server uses
stdlib net/http rather than x/net's
http2 — bumped to close the same
advisories on the module path)
Every fixed version above was read from that advisory's own page on
pkg.go.dev/vuln, not inferred. So an entry here still means what it says:
a finding that genuinely cannot be fixed, with a dated reason.
